meta.title: Reproducing Chloe: does the instruction-tuning mix matter?
meta.subtitle: Chloe's released model trains on Opus trait data plus a general instruction-tuning (IT) mix; our earlier runs omitted it. We reconstructed the exact IT mix from public datasets and trained the full recipe. Question: does adding the IT mix change where the model lands? Capability = GPQA-Diamond strict@20k thinking-on (n=198). Misalignment = canonical AM: agentic-misalignment murder (sonnet cascade, n=100) plus exfiltration (gpt-4.1, n=300), co-measured in one batch.
meta.y_label: misalignment (murder + exfiltration) → lower is more aligned

conditions.label: base (Qwen3-32B)
conditions.note: No adapter. The capability ceiling and misalignment floor we try not to drift back toward.

conditions.label: Chloe — released checkpoint
conditions.note: Her released model organism. Same low murder as our retrains, but it uniquely carries an exfiltration behavior, which is the whole gap.

conditions.label: Repro — trait data only
conditions.note: SFT on the Opus philosophy-spec tokens only, no instruction-tuning mix. What our earlier runs used.

conditions.label: Repro — + instruction mix
conditions.note: The full recipe: Opus trait tokens plus the reconstructed 10k IT mix (rendered per-sample thinking-off so it doesn't collapse reasoning).

notes: The IT mix barely moves the point. Trait-only (AM 0.018 / GPQA 0.48) and the full recipe with the IT mix (AM 0.027 / GPQA 0.51) land at the same place within noise. Adding the instruction-tuning data does not change where the model ends up, so the earlier no-IT runs were a fair stand-in.

Our retrains and the released checkpoint match on murder (all low: 0.03 to 0.06). The whole difference between them is exfiltration: the released checkpoint sits at 0.153 while both our retrains are about 0.01. So on the full misalignment axis our retrains are more aligned than the release, and the gap is entirely this one behavior.

The exfiltration gap is real, not batch noise. The release reproduces its standing value (0.153 vs a prior 0.147) and our no-IT arm reproduces its standing value (0.018 vs 0.027) across batches. The released checkpoint genuinely carries an exfiltration behavior our method-repro does not install.

Misalignment is co-measured for the trained arms in one eval batch. This matters because AM reads drift across batches (grader plus n plus setting noise), so only a single co-measured batch gives an honest ordering. GPQA is reproducible across batches (greedy, strict parse, no grader) so it is reused.

Getting the IT mix right required rendering the non-CoT instruction data with thinking off per-sample. Rendering everything thinking-on injects an empty think block on the IT samples and collapses the model to skip reasoning. That failed arm is excluded.

Recipe (all trained arms): Qwen3-32B, LoRA r64/alpha128, 1 epoch, lr 1e-4 cosine, seq 8192. IT mix = 10k samples (No Robots, Tulu3-IF, NuminaMath, smoltalk subsets, LIMA, LongAlign) reconstructed from public data at the published table counts.
